analysis:
This batch changes documentation only, in docs/reference/addon-hold-ipc.md and docs/reference/configuration.md. No executable code, key handling, attestation, encryption, or authorization logic changed. No finding qualifies.

Changed behavior is documented for the TB-012 / A-018 / T-059 add-on hold surface:
- addon-hold.json is opened with O_NONBLOCK and O_NOFOLLOW and read only as an owner-only regular file of at most 64 KiB. A FIFO or symlink is ignored as unreadable. This is a hardening description, not a regression.
- A 10 s per-line request timeout and an 8 KiB size cap are documented. Connections are limited to 8 verified, and a peer is verified at accept time before it takes a slot. These reduce slow-client and DoS exposure.
- Peer verification is documented as the LOCAL_PEERTOKEN audit token with an effective-UID match, a code requirement pinned to team SLDQ2GJ6TL and the io.darkbloom.sandbox identifier, and the hardened runtime. It is re-checked on every request.
- The DEBUG-only DARKBLOOM_ADDON_DEV_IDENTITY is documented as compiled out of release builds.
- DARKBLOOM_ADDON_SOCKET is documented as honored by every build but not passed through the LaunchAgent. This is an accurate disclosure. A same-UID local process that can set the provider's environment can already do much more, so this is not a new boundary.
- The settle-bound constant is renamed to addonHoldSettleTimeoutDefault, with a note that a load still running after the bound is waited for.

The addon-hold-ipc.md head text cites threat-model T-060. The supplied canonical index defines T-059 for TB-012 and has no T-060 entry. This may be a stale or forward reference, so the threat model needs a check for T-060 to avoid a dangling ID. It is documentation drift, not a security regression.

Source files (AddonIPC.swift, AddonIPCServer.swift, AddonPeerPolicy.swift, AddonHoldStore) were not supplied, so I could not verify the documented controls against code. The next pass should confirm the code enforces O_NOFOLLOW/O_NONBLOCK, the size cap, per-line timeout and per-request re-verification as documented.
